extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and Inter‑Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory; readers familiar with Frobenioids, log-volumes, and multiradial algorithms
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing the formation and properties of holomorphic/holomorphic-like 'hulls', their associated map φ, and the use of hull-approximants (Φ, Ξ) and determinant/tensor-power operations (det⊗M) to compare outputs of multiradial algorithms with arithmetic line-bundle/Frobenioid data via log-volume computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic hull ("hull") definition and well-definedness
rubrics_metrics.description: For a given object (e.g., αU, AU; A, αU) contained in I_Q((−)), if the object is not relatively compact then its holomorphic hull is defined to be I_Q(αFvQ) (respectively I_Q(AFvQ); I_Q(A,αFv)). One verifies immediately that the holomorphic hull is well-defined under the stated conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat 'holomorphic hulls' (short: 'hulls') as the canonical enlargement of a region to an element of H ⊆ P (direct product regions). The hull construction is the basic operation used to convert arbitrary regions into objects compatible with arithmetic/vector-bundle structure; see (ii)–(vii) for usage. If an object is already relatively compact, its hull is itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map φ : P → H properties (P1)-(P3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation of forming hulls determines a canonical map φ from the set P of direct product regions to H (the hulls), uniquely characterized by: (P1) φ(H) = H for any H ∈ H; (P2) P ⊆ φ(P) for any P ∈ P; (P3) If P1 ⊆ P2 then φ(P1) ⊆ φ(P2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: φ can be viewed as an adjoint/push-forward/splitting/integration of the inclusion H ⊆ P; equivalently φ(P) = intersection of all H ∈ H with H ⊇ P (finite log-volume intersections yield elements of H). Compatibility (P2),(P3) with pre-order by inclusion is essential for subsequent log-volume estimates and constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Φ(P) and Ξ(P): hull-based log-volume approximants
rubrics_metrics.description: For P ∈ P, define Φ(P) = {H ∈ H | φ(P) ⊇ H, μlog(φ(P)) ≥ μlog(H) ≥ μlog(P)} and Ξ(P) = {H ∈ H | φ(P) ⊇ H, μlog(H) = μlog(P)}. Also define HΦ(P) = ⋃_{H ∈ Φ(P)} H and HΞ(P) = ⋃_{H ∈ Ξ(P)} H (each subset of φ(P)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements of Φ(P) or Ξ(P) are 'log-volume approximations' (hull-approximants) of P. Use Φ(P) when Ξ(P) may be empty; working with these sets helps move from arbitrary regions to hulls that approximate log-volume while remaining within H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness of indeterminacy (all choices contained in φ(P))
rubrics_metrics.description: The indeterminacy in choosing an element of Φ(P) or Ξ(P) is compact: all possible choices are contained in the compact hull φ(P) ∈ H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design constructions so that all indeterminacies arising in assignments (e.g., choosing a specific hull-approximant) are contained in compact sets. The compactness would fail if the condition 'H ⊆ φ(P)' were omitted from the definitions of Φ(P) or Ξ(P). This compactness is a central theme of the series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonemptiness criteria for Ξ(P) (Ξ1, Ξ2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain conditions Ξ(P) is nonempty. Two sufficient conditions given are: (Ξnon1) if K^cl is the Galois closure of K/Q and the residue field extension degree of each valuation over v_Q in V(K^cl) dividing v_Q ∈ V_non equals 1, and μlog(P)=μlog(Q) for some Q ∈ P which is a Z_pvQ-submodule of I_Q((−)); (Ξarc1) if v_Q ∈ V_arc; additionally (Ξ2) in global situations (varying v_Q) the global analogue of Ξ(P) is nonempty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These give concrete arithmetic/geometric hypotheses under which exact log-volume-preserving hulls exist. However, in general it is not clear whether Ξ(P) ≠ ∅, so one must often work with Φ(P) instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-volume inequality can be strict; need to compare μlog(P) and μlog(φ(P))
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when P ⊆ φ(P), the induced inequality of log-volumes μlog(P) ≤ μlog(HΦ(P)) = μlog(φ(P)) can be strict. An explicit p-adic example (I = Q_p×Q_p, H0 = Z_p×Z_p, etc.) shows μ_I(P) = 1 < 2 − p^{−1} = μ_I(H0 ∪ H1) so μlog(P) < μlog(HΦ(P)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect that passing to hulls can increase log-volume; computations and comparisons must account for this. Examples illustrate that φ(P) (the hull) may strictly enlarge log-volume compared to P.

rubrics_metrics.name: (cid:11)-formalism: quotienting to eliminate hull-indeterminacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a set E and subset S of cardinality ≥2, the quotient E/S (identifying elements of S) induces a formalism in which maps between subsets of S descend to identity maps on the image point {S} in the quotient, and formal inverse systems including empty intersections map to {S}. Applied to hulls, this lets one identify P with its various hull-approximants inside φ(P), eliminating indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the set-theoretic quotient identification (treating φ(P) as S) to collapse the internal indeterminacy among elements H ⊆ φ(P); this is a tool to produce coarse/set-theoretic invariants and to enable comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to bounded families PB: use φ(PB) to control family indeterminacy
rubrics_metrics.description: For a bounded family PB = {P_β} (∪ P_β relatively compact), define φ(PB) = ⋂_{H ⊇ P_β ∀β} H ⊆ I_Q((−)). The (cid:11)-formalism with S = φ(PB) identifies each P_β with its hull-approximants and eliminates family-wide indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend the quotient formalism to families of regions to obtain simultaneous identifications and ensure uniform control of indeterminacies for collections of outputs of multiradial algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ob1: O×-Indeterminacies on tensor packets of log-shells
rubrics_metrics.description: The outputs of multiradial algorithms are regions ∈ P contained in tensor packets of log-shells I_k. By contrast, the arithmetic line bundle giving rise to the q-pilot object appears locally as an Ok-module Omdl which does not admit a canonical generator; Ik is defined using the ring Ok and is not stabilized by multiplication by O×_k. Thus multiplication by O×_k induces an indeterminacy that does not stabilize Ik.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the lack of canonical generators (only canonical up to O×) creates an O×-indeterminacy; to compare algorithm outputs to arithmetic line bundles one must pass to structures (hulls) stabilized by the O×-action (see Ob2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ob2: From arbitrary regions to arithmetic vector bundles via hulls
rubrics_metrics.description: By passing from an arbitrary region P ∈ P to the associated hull φ(P) ∈ H one obtains a region stabilized by O×_k and which may be regarded as defining the local portion of a global arithmetic vector bundle relative to a chosen ring label α ∈ A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form hulls to obtain objects that have the necessary multiplicative invariance (stabilized by units) and hence can be treated as arithmetic vector bundles (local pieces of arithmetic geometry objects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ob3: From arithmetic vector bundles to arithmetic line bundles via det⊗M(−)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming determinants of arithmetic vector bundles (hulls) yields arithmetic line bundles appropriate for comparison with q-pilot objects, but to match log-volume computations one must perform weighted tensor powers and normalization (denoted det⊗M(−)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key subpoints: (Ob3-1) use suitable positive tensor powers corresponding to weights to make determinant consistent with log-volume sums; (Ob3-1-1) form weighted determinants of direct summands; (Ob3-1-2) tensor with inverse determinant of structure sheaf O(−) to adjust for ramification; (Ob3-2) positive tensor powers need not be relatively prime; denote M the suitable positive integer and work with M-th tensor powers so localizations become trivial for sufficiently divisible M; (Ob3-3) arithmetic degree of the resulting line bundle can be interpreted as the log-volume up to normalization, so in pure log-volume discussions det⊗M may be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ob4: Positive tensor powers and tensor-power Frobenioids (tensor-power indeterminacies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying det⊗M(−) yields objects comparable to those in the LGP-prime-strip codomain but corresponding to M-th tensor powers of the q-pilot object. The tensor-power Frobenioids determine the non-tensor-power Frobenioids via naive Frobenius functors of degree M, but recovering non-tensor-power objects introduces twists (tensor-power-twist indeterminacies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoints: (Ob4-1) naive Frobenius functor of degree M converts non-tensor-power Frobenioids to tensor-power versions; (Ob4-2) conversely extracting M-th roots recovers non-tensor-power Frobenioids only up to twists because rational function monoids are not divisible at v∈V_non; (Ob4-3) tensor-power-twist indeterminacies do not affect log-volume estimates and can be controlled by appropriate functorial constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ob5: Independence from choice of internal possibilities — use hulls φ(PB)
rubrics_metrics.description: To compare outputs of multiradial algorithms (collections of possible regions PB) with external arithmetic objects (q-pilot), one must use objects independent of the internal choice of a specific possible region. This is achieved by working with the hull φ(PB) of the bounded collection PB and applying the (cid:11)-formalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use φ(PB) to obtain invariants independent of arbitrary algorithmic choices; the same formalism applies compatibly to det⊗M(φ(PB)) and μlog(φ(PB)). This eliminates internal choice-dependence in comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ob6: Use hull-approximants (Φ(P), Ξ(P)) for log-volume comparisons; prefer Φ(P) when Ξ(P) uncertain
rubrics_metrics.description: Although one might be tempted to replace a region P by its log-volume μlog(P), to obtain objects comparable with q-pilot objects one is obliged to work with hulls ∈ H. Thus consider Ξ(P) (exact-volume hulls) or, more generally, Φ(P) (approximate-volume hulls). Since Ξ(P) may be empty in general, Φ(P) is often the natural choice; ultimately one must consider μlog(HΦ(P)) or μlog(HΞ(P)) rather than μlog(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer Φ(P) for robust approximations; remember μlog(HΦ(P)) can exceed μlog(P). The nonemptiness of Ξ(P) is a delicate arithmetic question (see Ξ1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ob7: Necessity of F^(3)×μ-prime-strip data (local Galois groups and units) — compatibility with log-Kummer
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot eliminate the F^(3)×μ-prime-strip portion (concretely: local Galois groups G_v and Frobenius-like units O×^μ_F_v) from the F^(4)(5)×μ-prime-strips that appear in the Θ-LGP-link. The local Galois groups are invariant (up to iso) under Θ-LGP and log-links (coricity properties) and are essential. The Frobenius-like units differ fundamentally from the étale-like units and cannot be replaced without over-constraining the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two key reasons: (Ob7-1) local Galois groups' coricity/invariance is essential for relating objects under Θ- and log-links; (Ob7-2) replacing Frobenius-like units with étale-like units introduces vertical-coricity-induced relations across vertical coordinates, causing over-constraint/incompatibility with the intended intrinsic splittings between unit and value-group portions. Keep both local Galois group and unit data in the prime-strip structures to preserve log-Kummer and log-shell theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ob8: Vertical shifts — log-Kummer correspondences and iterates of the log-link
rubrics_metrics.description: Output of multiradial algorithms (even after passing to hulls) may yield objects in Frobenioids that differ from the corresponding input Frobenioids by a 'vertical shift' in the log-theta-lattice. Log-Kummer correspondences transport/relate outputs to different vertical coordinates; comparable objects are obtained by applying log-Kummer but are then subject to indeterminacies given by arbitrary iterates of the log-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To compare outputs and inputs one must apply log-Kummer correspondences to adjust vertical coordinates; expect indeterminacy from iterates of the log-link, which must be accounted for in any comparison or invariants built thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ob9: Compatibility of hulls with the log-link and log-volumes; role of realified semi-simplications
rubrics_metrics.description: Passing to realified semi-simplications (quotients) in contexts involving the log-link yields a quotient on both domain and codomain that induces a natural bijection between log-volumes of hulls in domain and codomain. The formal/stack-theoretic indeterminacies (tensor-power twists, (cid:11)-formalism, iterates of the log-link) then act only as compatibility conditions when passing to coarse invariants like log-volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After passing to comparable objects (via det⊗M and hulls), the formal indeterminacies no longer affect comparability of coarse invariants (Ob9-1). Before this final step, relationships between non-comparable and comparable objects may be non-explicit (Ob9-2). Use realified semi-simplications to obtain bijective correspondence of log-volumes across log-link transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: (sQ1)-(sQ5) collection: (sub)quotient operation algorithms for simplifying the log-theta-lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: The operations Kummer-detachment (sQ1), Galois evaluation (sQ2), passing from regions to positive tensor powers of determinants of hulls and applying the (cid:11)-formalism (sQ3), adjusting vertical shifts via log-Kummer (sQ4), and passing to log-volumes via realified semi-simplications (sQ5) are viewed as (sub)quotient/push-forward/splitting/integration operations that simplify the full log-theta-lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each operation introduces indeterminacies; the nontrivial content is balancing minimizing indeterminacies while ensuring compatibility with prior structures. Detailed delicate issues: (sQ1) Kummer-detachment subtleties (see remarks cited); (sQ2) compatibility with Kummer theory when doing Galois evaluation; (sQ3) tensor-power-twist and (cid:11)-formalism issues; (sQ4) vertical-shift indeterminacies from iterated log-links; (sQ5) compatibility of log-volume with log-link. The overall goal is to compute the projection of 'Θ-intertwining' onto the 'q-intertwining' via these controlled subquotient operations (culminating in Corollary 3.12 inequality).
